A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same forePLay dataset and model evaluation. Their main text, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renamed material.

before.justification: v1 reports original corpus statistics, annotation-agreement analyses, classification scores, and model refusal counts in Sections 3–6.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds class-specific error counts and an aggregate error analysis in Section 7 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The taxonomy, annotation aggregation, model architectures, and fine-tuning/prompting approaches are retained. Appendix B corrects the violence-label guideline to match the definition already present in v1 Section 4.1; it does not establish a changed annotation procedure or relabeling.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 24,768-sentence Polish corpus using Basic, Core, Extended, and Full label configurations. The newly described 3,704-sentence public release concerns access; no separate training or evaluation on that subset is reported.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set is retained, with standardized PLLuM names. The Bielik score-row label changes from v2.2 to v2.3, matching v1 Section 5.3 and Table 7; identical scores and retained descriptions support a naming correction rather than an established model replacement.

E3.justification: The added error analysis introduces per-class false-positive/false-negative counts and an FP/(FP+FN) summary metric. Existing F1 results are explicitly identified as macro-F1, with unchanged values; the PDFs do not establish changes to the original splits, training budgets, or evaluation runs.

E4.justification: v3 adds a systematic error analysis across all four dataset configurations, classes, and inference settings through Figure 1 and Appendix D. This substantially extends the retained annotation-disagreement and refusal analyses by examining false-positive and false-negative patterns.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 1 newly displays error bars identified as 95% confidence intervals. Their construction and any repeated-run or seed counts are unspecified, so this establishes additional uncertainty reporting, not additional experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: Tables 8–11 add extensive class-specific error results and Figure 1 adds aggregate findings. For example, Table 11 reports 115 false positives and one false negative for GPT-4o on Basic in zero-shot evaluation. Matched original classification scores, refusal counts, corpus statistics, and agreement values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 Section 7 introduces the mathematical definition of its 'Type I error percentage' as FP/(FP+FN), absent from v1. This is a limited addition of a defined quantity; neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: the first manually annotated Polish erotic-content dataset, its multidimensional taxonomy, and the claimed advantages of Polish-specialized models and encoders on imbalanced categories.

C2.justification: v3 adds a precision/sensitivity interpretation of the new error analysis and acknowledges that omitting label definitions from prompts may explain weaker model performance. It also clarifies applications to platform-specific moderation policies beyond legal requirements. Existing discussion and limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v1's future-release promise becomes a dataset link and a reported release of 2,728 erotic and 976 ambiguous sentences, explicitly excluding neutral and both harmful classes. v3 also expands source-selection and annotator-role details, specifies context-free sentence presentation, and corrects Appendix B. Computational settings are retained in the relocated Appendix E.

R1.justification: The cited research works and related-work discussion are retained. Added PLLuM access links do not introduce new research comparisons or substantively revise the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes focused revisions to the abstract, introduction, and annotation description, standardizes terminology, and reformats the annotation guidelines. It adds Data Availability and Acknowledgements sections and inserts an error-analysis appendix, while retaining most prose and the main narrative structure.

P2.justification: v3 adds a grouped error chart with confidence intervals and four detailed error tables. Existing tables are reordered and relocated, captions move below tables, and the retained prompt panel is compressed and renumbered. These substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through corrected annotation guidelines, fuller provenance, and documented partial data access. However, the new error analysis introduces reliability concerns: FP/(FP+FN) does not directly measure precision or false-positive rate, its claimed 40–50% Full result conflicts with Figure 1's roughly 52–57% bars, and Table 11 contains a missing error count. Confidence-interval construction is unexplained. With the central performance evidence unchanged, these documentation gains and new analytical weaknesses prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
